ai.description: *Amolops monticola* is a 4–6 cm frog with a green to brown dorsum and dark mottling. It features expanded, truncate finger discs and a distinct, white supralabial stripe. It inhabits fast-flowing streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops monticola* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad, and continuous pale dorsolateral fold that contrasts sharply with its dark, mottled back.
ai.habitat: *Amolops monticola* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky hill streams within subtropical and temperate forests, typically at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mountain Cascade Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively foraging for small insects along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of its high-altitude habitat after dark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops monticola* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in mountain streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically producing small clutches of aquatic eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops monticola* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and West Bengal, at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Mountain Cascade Frog emits a series of high-pitched, piercing whistles while perched on rocks near the rushing water of fast-flowing mountain streams.
